Test fitted effects

Source: R/effects.R
test_effect.Rd

Tests the null hypothesis that a functional returned by estimate_effect() is zero. The arguments select the same terms, compositions, groupings, and groups. One test is returned per selected term and grouping level.

Usage

test_effect(
  object,
  terms = NULL,
  axes = list(),
  impulses = NULL,
  responses = NULL,
  composition = c("term", "total"),
  grouping = c("population", "deviation", "conditional"),
  groups = NULL,
  reference = list(),
  unconditional = FALSE,
  n = 50L,
  tolerance = 1e-08,
  boundary = c("estimate", "bound"),
  points = NULL,
  method = c("wood", "wald")
)

Arguments

object

A fitted cdrgam model.

terms

Term labels, or a selector list with optional fields names (term labels), predictors (predictor names, or "*" for any term with predictors), match ("contains", the default, or "exact"), and grouped (logical). NULL selects every impulse-response term.

axes

Named axis requests. Predictor requests are nested under predictors; "*" supplies a fallback for every predictor axis.

impulses, responses

Optional training streams used to recover axis summaries from models fitted before summaries were stored.

composition

Return the selected term alone or add its hierarchy of fitted marginal terms.

grouping

Return population, grouped-deviation, or conditional effects.

groups

Optional grouping levels.

reference

Optional named list of reference values for evaluation axes, using the same request forms as axes. Each request must resolve to one value. A predictor may instead be NA or "default" to leave it at the model default. Names are axis names such as lag or a predictor.

unconditional

Include smoothing-parameter uncertainty when supported. Smoothing parameters classified as on the boundary of their range contribute no uncertainty, because the criterion has no local curvature along them. Sparse fits stop with an error when the outer Hessian is not positive definite after those parameters are excluded.

n

Default number of points for fitted-domain grids.

tolerance

Relative eigenvalue threshold for the rank of L V L' under method = "wald".

boundary

"estimate" (the default) uses the fitted smoothing parameters. "bound" repeats the calculation with each boundary smoothing parameter set to its profile bound, the largest variance component the data still support, while the other smoothing parameters stay at their estimates. Compare the two to check whether conclusions depend on treating those variance components as zero. "bound" requires a sparse Gaussian REML fit with sparse_control$boundary_sensitivity = TRUE and unconditional = FALSE.

points

Optional data frame of evaluation points, one per row, with columns named by axis, such as lag or a predictor. Its columns are paired rather than crossed, so the result has one row per point. Each axis that is not a column takes its value from axes, and that request must resolve to one value. Use it to evaluate along a path through the axes, such as each predictor value at its own lag.

method

"wood" for Wood's whole-functional test or "wald" for a grid Wald test. When omitted, it is "wald" if axes, reference, or points define a grid and "wood" otherwise.

Value

A cdrgam_effect_test data frame with term_id, term, group, composition, grouping, method, statistic, df, residual_df, p_value, points, and coefficients. residual_df is missing for chi-squared references, and points for Wood tests. Under method = "wald", df is zero and statistic and p_value are missing when the functional is identically zero.

Details

method = "wood" tests the whole functional, as summary() tests smooth terms. The null is that every coefficient the functional uses is zero, so a total composition is tested over the union of its terms' coefficients. The statistic is Wood's (2013), with the summed alternative effective degrees of freedom of those coefficients as its reference rank. A functional made of exactly one fully penalized term, such as a grouped deviation, gets Wood's (2013b) random-effect test, with other random effects integrated out. Grouped deviations are therefore tested over all levels at once, and groups must be NULL. The test does not use an evaluation grid, so axes, reference, and points must be empty. When the scale is estimated, statistic is the F statistic T / df on df and residual_df degrees of freedom, as in summary(); otherwise it is T on a chi-squared reference.

method = "wald" tests the functional at every point of an evaluation grid. The statistic is \(\hat\beta^\top L^\top (L V L^\top)^{-} L \hat\beta\), where L stacks the grid rows of the functional and V is the coefficient covariance. The pseudo-inverse keeps eigenvalues above tolerance times the largest, and the reference distribution is chi-squared with that rank as its degrees of freedom. Use a grid dense enough to span the functional; the rank stops growing once it does. This test can reject too rarely when the null holds on the boundary of the smoothing-parameter space (Wood 2013).

References

Wood, S. N. (2013). On p-values for smooth components of an extended generalized additive model. Biometrika, 100(1), 221–228.

Wood, S. N. (2013b). A simple test for random effects in regression models. Biometrika, 100(4), 1005–1010.
